ref_date_note: All numbers ESZ5/NQZ5 (letter: 'I am now using ESZ/NQZ levels moving forward'). Typos read literally-corrected: NQ weekly '24722-22740' -> 24722-24740; '480-793' -> 24780-24793. The rotational paragraph (edges ES 6687-6690/6707-6710, NQ 24722-24740/24780-24793) is split into four trades with the grades he assigns: ES long A/A- (es1), ES short C+/B- (es2), NQ long B/B+ (nq1), NQ short C+/B- (nq2), all quoting the same paragraph. es3 (LBAF of 6687-6690, A/A+) overlaps es1 - it is the upgraded version. 'LBAF of today's low on either' (B/B+) -> es4 and nq3, gated RTH_LOW (no number given); ES today's low is below 6681 and above 6666-6669, NQ today's low is near 24600 (held Tuesday's high), so their targets are the next commentary levels above. nq4/es5 lower-high shorts are ungraded ('can consider'); gated on the zone and kind=break like 'lower high below X'. The LAAF of today's high on either index is explicitly not planned ('I won't plan on this short') -> not transcribed. SPX 6666-6669 mention is SPX, not ES. 'rally into the 24800s' not recorded as a level.

trades.name: Rotational long: hold/LBAF of lower edge 6687-6690
trades.quote: The rotational trading on either ES or NQ mentioned above, broadly favoring longs as buyers are in control. The ES lower edge is perhaps more clean than NQ, and NQ was a tad heavier late today so I may prefer to long ES in these situations. Shorts are valid, just not preferred, as long as price is rotating (or better sees a failed break) between these edges and there is a reversal into a downtrend, or one has compelling order flow reasons to get short. I would rate the ES long as an A/A-, the NQ long as a B/B+, and shorts on either as a C+/B-.
